scope: Proposition 5.2 (An escape estimate from the uniform start) of the manuscript “Universality of critical quench autocorrelations in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Universality-of-critical-quench-autocorrelations-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-October-5-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 12d511db42d09b8c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 58. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a measurable admissible choice b = b(g) such that, almost surely, ra := ga + b > 0, Dg(b) > 0, cg(1 + a)2/3 ≤ ra ≤ Cg(1 + a)2/3 (a ≥ 1) (5.16) for finite positive cg, Cg. Define Mg(x) = 1 2 X a≥1 x2 a ra . (5.17) Then 0 < Mg < ∞ Πg-almost surely. Choose a Borel full-measure set of edge realizations on which these assertions about b, ra, and Mg hold, with b Borel there and ra = ga + b. On the product of this edge set with RN, Mg is an extended nonnegative Borel function of (g, x), since its jointly Borel partial sums increase to it. In every escape event, x2 i /Mg(x) denotes the quotient on the subset where 0 < Mg(x) < ∞, extended by zero to all remaining pairs in RN × RN. This version is jointly Borel and agrees with the usual quotient Πg-almost surely for every g in the chosen edge set. For every represented family in Proposition 5.1, every fixed i ≥ 1, and every ϵ > 0, lim s↓0 b E h Πg h hs1{x2 i /Mg>ϵ} ii = 0. (5.18) Here the probability averages the represented environment as well as the draw from hsΠg.
